Learning starts with a conversation.

A family guide to choosing activities, finding useful resources and supporting independent study.

On this page

Getting startedCommon questionsFamily tools

Begin with the learner.

Ask what they are curious about, what feels difficult and what they would like to make. Choose one suitable pathway activity together, agree on a manageable time and revisit the plan after a week.

Our age bands are flexible suggestions. A younger learner may need adult guidance, and an older learner may benefit from revisiting a foundation.

Explore learning pathways

Before you begin.

Do these resources lead to qualifications?

No. These open materials support independent learning. They do not offer enrollment, academic credit, school records or qualifications.

Can we use the guides at home?

Yes. The suggestions are available to read without an account. Choose materials suited to the learner, provide appropriate adult support and check the rights of external resources.

Is there an application form or a fee?

No. This site has no application process, tuition payments or donation collection. You do not need to share personal, financial or student details to use these resources.

Where can we get help with actual coursework?

Use your real school’s established channels to contact a teacher, counselor or administrator. A local library can also help you choose suitable learning materials.
